$comment: Rule catalog — split. Standards 5, 10, 14. How data is partitioned, and the discipline that keeps a held-out estimate honest. split.no-test-set-tuning carries two source statements — tuning against the final test set, and repeatedly inspecting it until model choices fit — because they are one conceptual prohibition reached by two routes; both are reproduced verbatim, in Standards 14 and 5 respectively.

rules.title: Three roles are declared and held by different partitions
rules.description: Training, validation, and test roles are declared explicitly, and no partition holds two of them. The separation is over the unit of prediction rather than over rows, so that related observations cannot straddle a boundary.
rules.rationale: The test set's entire value is that the process has never adapted to it. A partition serving two roles has adapted to itself, and the estimate it produces is optimistic by an amount nobody can quantify.
rules.remediation: Declare the three partitions, separate the test set first, and check that the split key is the unit of prediction rather than the row index.
rules.evidenceExpected: Split code or configuration showing three distinct partitions and the key they are split on, with an attestation that no observation's group spans a boundary.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. Whether a split key is the correct unit of prediction depends on what an observation means, which is not in the code.

rules.title: The final test set is never a selection signal
rules.description: No model choice may be made in light of the final test set. This covers automated search scored against it and the slower human version — repeatedly inspecting it and adjusting until the choices fit. Standard 5 P1 and Standard 14 P1 are the two source statements of this one prohibition.
rules.rationale: Each look at the test set transfers information from it into the model, and the resulting estimate becomes optimistic by an amount that cannot be measured because measuring it would require an untouched test set. The damage is cumulative and silent.
rules.remediation: Move the selection signal to validation data or an inner cross-validation loop. Where the test set has already driven choices, it is no longer a held-out set: obtain fresh data before reporting a generalisation estimate, and say what happened.
rules.evidenceExpected: A search procedure scored against validation data, plus an attestation recording how many times the test set was examined and whether any choice followed from it.
rules.$assuranceNote: The check detects a fit-family call whose arguments carry conventionally test-named identifiers. It finds a naming convention and nothing more: a test set named holdout2 is invisible, and the repeated-inspection half of this prohibition is not code at all. Absence of a finding establishes nothing.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: Non-exemptible. A spent test set cannot be unspent, so no waiver restores the evidence the tuning destroyed — an exception here would approve a number that has already stopped meaning what it says.

rules.title: The fold scheme is derived from the data's dependence structure
rules.description: Where cross-validation is used, the fold scheme is chosen from the data's dependence structure — independent, grouped, or time-ordered — and the choice is recorded with its reason.
rules.rationale: Cross-validation stabilises an estimate only when the folds respect the structure of the data. A scheme chosen by default rather than by analysis produces a tighter and more confident number that is wrong in the same direction every time.
rules.remediation: Determine whether observations are grouped or time-ordered, select the matching splitter, and record why. Fit every transformation inside each fold rather than once over the whole dataset.
rules.evidenceExpected: A recorded determination of the data's dependence structure and the splitter chosen to match it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. Inferring that data is temporal or grouped from column names was considered and rejected: it fails in both directions, and a pass would assert that the scheme had been reviewed.

rules.title: Temporal and grouped data are not shuffled into folds
rules.description: A cross-validation scheme must not ignore dependence the data has. Random folds over grouped observations evaluate the model on entities it has effectively seen; random folds over time-ordered observations train on the future.
rules.rationale: The failure is invisible in the result — it produces a better score, not a worse one — so nothing about the output prompts anyone to look for it.
rules.remediation: Replace the splitter with one that matches the structure: grouped folds for entity-level dependence, forward-chaining folds for time order.
rules.evidenceExpected: An attestation that the fold scheme was checked against the data's dependence structure, naming the code reviewed.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this, for the same reason as split.cv-scheme-justified: the dependence structure is a property of what the data means.
